title: WordStar: A Writer's Word Processor (1996)
summary: A nostalgic 1996 article praising WordStar, a DOS-era word processor known for its efficient keyboard-driven interface and minimalist design that many writers found superior for long-form content creation over modern GUI-based alternatives.
problem_solved: Provides efficient, distraction-free keyboard-driven text editing for writers in the pre-GUI computing era.
why_valuable: Documents a timeless minimalist approach to writing software that emphasizes focus and productivity, offering insights into why some writers still prefer keyboard-centric tools.
